hints: Think about the job of each place separately, the engine burns fuel while the converter cleans up pollutants.
Remember that burning petrol in the engine gives complete combustion products plus pollutants like CO, unburnt hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides.
Now ask which harmless products are made when the converter oxidises CO and unburnt hydrocarbons, and check which of those were also made in the engine.
walkthrough:
**What the car engine produces**

In the engine, petrol combusts in air. Complete combustion gives the main products.

$$\text{hydrocarbon} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Incomplete combustion and high temperature also give pollutants: $\text{CO}$, unburnt hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides ($\text{NO}_x$).

**What the catalytic converter produces**

The converter is designed to remove pollutants by converting them into harmless substances. Carbon monoxide is oxidised, unburnt hydrocarbons are oxidised, and nitrogen oxides are reduced.

$$2\text{CO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{hydrocarbon} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$2\text{NO} \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Find the overlap**

Compare the two lists. The engine makes $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ as main combustion products. The converter also makes $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ when it oxidises $\text{CO}$ and unburnt hydrocarbons. These are the only pair made in both places.

options.A: Carbon dioxide is made in both places, but unburnt hydrocarbons are only made in the engine. In the converter they are reactants that are used up, not products.
options.B: Correct. Complete combustion in the engine produces carbon dioxide and water. Oxidation of CO and of unburnt hydrocarbons in the catalytic converter also produces carbon dioxide and water. So this pair is produced in both.
options.C: Carbon monoxide is made in the engine but it is removed (used up) in the converter, not produced there. Nitrogen is made in the converter from NOx, but the engine makes nitrogen oxides, not nitrogen.
options.D: Both carbon monoxide and unburnt hydrocarbons are pollutants made in the engine. The whole purpose of the converter is to consume them, so they are reactants there, not products.
